help.findings.what: Combines the findings from Trivy and OSV into one list: actively exploited vulnerabilities (KEV) first, then by exploitation likelihood (EPSS), then by severity.
help.findings.why: Two scanners produce hundreds of findings. The order puts what is urgent on top.
help.findings.ours: Appears daily at 08:00 in the daily report in Slack and here. The severities (CRITICAL to LOW) come from the CVSS rating of the vulnerability.
help.trivy.what: Trivy is an open-source scanner. It checks the images of our running containers for known vulnerabilities (CVEs) in operating system packages and libraries.
help.trivy.why: Every image brings its own packages, which the nightly server patching does not reach. Without a scan we do not see these vulnerabilities.
help.trivy.ours: Daily: the collector on each server asks the trivy-server on the ops server. If the report is missing for more than 26 hours or the scan fails, a P2 opens.
help.osv.what: osv-scanner checks the lockfiles of our repos against the open vulnerability database OSV.
help.osv.why: Finds vulnerable libraries in the code, before they are built and shipped.
help.osv.ours: Every night at 02:30 the repos are cloned read-only and scanned. If a repo cannot be read, a P2 opens.
help.intel.what: KEV is the list of vulnerabilities that are known to be exploited, kept by the US agency CISA. EPSS estimates the probability that a vulnerability is exploited in the next 30 days.
help.intel.why: We use them to decide what gets patched first: an exploited vulnerability before one that is only theoretically severe.
help.intel.ours: Daily at 06:00 for all CVEs that Trivy or OSV found. A KEV hit opens a P1 immediately, per vulnerability and server or repo. If a feed is unreachable, the last state applies and a P2 opens.
help.patch.what: unattended-upgrades installs the Ubuntu security updates at 03:00, needrestart restarts the affected services.
help.patch.why: Operating system vulnerabilities are closed overnight without anyone stepping in. The report shows whether it worked.
help.patch.ours: At 03:40 the collector reports what was installed and restarted, and whether the services answer afterwards. If the report is missing for more than 26 hours, a P2 opens.
help.reboot.what: Some updates, a new kernel for example, only take effect after a reboot.
help.reboot.why: A reboot interrupts the service for a moment. So a person decides whether and when.
help.reboot.ours: If the patch window reports that a reboot is needed, the ops service asks in Slack "Reboot on Sunday at 04:00?". Without approval nothing happens.
help.backup.what: Checks through the Coolify API whether the Postgres backups ran and arrived in S3.
help.backup.why: A backup that fails silently is only noticed when you try to restore.
help.backup.ours: Every 30 minutes. P1 if no backup succeeded for 26 hours. P2 if the last one failed, is only half the size of the one before, or is not in S3.
help.lynis.what: Lynis checks the server configuration against known hardening rules and gives an index from 0 to 100.
help.lynis.why: We follow the index over the weeks so that no decline creeps in.
help.lynis.ours: Every Sunday at 04:30. If the report is missing for more than 8 days, a P2 opens.
help.crowdsec.what: CrowdSec detects attack patterns in the server logs, such as password guessing or scans, and bans the IP addresses.
help.crowdsec.why: Automated attacks run around the clock. Bans happen immediately, the report shows what was going on.
help.crowdsec.ours: Daily report with attacks and active bans. If it is missing for more than 26 hours, a P2 opens.
help.ssh.what: Checks every SSH login on the servers: key, user and origin.
help.ssh.why: A foreign login is the clearest sign that someone got in.
help.ssh.ours: Daily. Known keys (fingerprint, user, network) count as usual. Everything else comes as one grouped message per server in the ops channel; an unknown key, or a known key used by the wrong user or from the wrong network, gets a message of its own.
help.images.what: Compares every running image with the registry, following the approach of Diun, and the Coolify version with the latest release.
help.images.why: Shows where an update is due. The update itself stays an action with approval.
help.images.ours: Every night at 04:30. Images that are built on the server cannot be checked this way and show up as "not checkable".
help.runner.what: The ops-runner runs on the app server and carries out the actions you approve in Slack: restart a container, clean up images, security updates, scheduled reboot. It asks the ops service every 10 seconds; every request is its sign of life.
help.runner.why: A runner that no longer asks carries out no approval, exactly when you need one. It also sits on the server that is exposed to the internet, so it checks every job for signature, catalog, server and deadline.
help.runner.ours: If it does not report for 3 minutes, a P1 opens (RunnerSilent). While an action is running it counts as active. If its catalog differs from the catalog of the service, it rejects every job; the card warns then.
